## 1. Purpose

This module freezes the input contract for the real *Coffea arabica* genomic-prediction workflow. It reads the prepared genotype and phenotype objects already present in `data/dados_reais/`, verifies their alignment, applies the prespecified marker quality-control rules, summarizes the three prediction traits, and saves one common object consumed by all downstream real-data modules.

The module deliberately does **not** reconstruct undocumented historical preprocessing steps that produced older marker panels. The canonical analysis starts from the current aligned RDS objects and applies transparent quality-control rules defined here.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  cache = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "100%"
)

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

dir.create(
  "output/real/audit",
  showWarnings = FALSE,
  recursive = TRUE
)
```

## 2. Packages

```{r packages, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(knitr)
```

## 3. Canonical prepared inputs

```{r read-inputs}
geno_raw <- readRDS(
  "data/dados_reais/geno_real.rds"
)

pheno <- readRDS(
  "data/dados_reais/pheno_real.rds"
)

G <- as.matrix(geno_raw)

input_summary <- data.frame(
  Object = c("geno_real.rds", "pheno_real.rds"),
  Rows = c(nrow(G), nrow(pheno)),
  Columns = c(ncol(G), ncol(pheno)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

input_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Canonical prepared real-data inputs",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

The prepared objects contain 195 individuals. The genotype matrix contains the marker panel available before the transparent quality-control step implemented below, while the phenotype object contains the three prediction traits used by the real-data workflow.

## 4. Individual alignment

```{r alignment-audit}
required_traits <- c("Prod.Cor", "Cer", "BM")

alignment_checks <- data.frame(
  Check = c(
    "Same number of individuals",
    "Genotype row names equal phenotype labels in the same order",
    "Unique genotype row names",
    "Unique phenotype labels",
    "Required prediction traits available",
    "No missing values in prediction traits"
  ),
  Passed = c(
    nrow(G) == nrow(pheno),
    identical(rownames(G), pheno$genotipo),
    !anyDuplicated(rownames(G)),
    !anyDuplicated(pheno$genotipo),
    all(required_traits %in% names(pheno)),
    all(vapply(pheno[required_traits], function(x) all(!is.na(x)), logical(1)))
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

alignment_checks |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Individual and phenotype alignment checks",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )

stopifnot(all(alignment_checks$Passed))
```

The row order is therefore part of the frozen contract: each genotype row corresponds directly to the phenotype row carrying the same `genotipo` label.

## 5. Population structure

The 195 analyzed individuals belong to 13 progenies with 15 individuals per progeny. Family membership is derived only from the stable individual label, for example `PROG 10_4` belongs to `PROG 10`.

```{r family-structure}
family <- sub("_.*$", "", pheno$genotipo)
family_size <- sort(table(family))

family_table <- data.frame(
  Family = names(family_size),
  N = as.integer(family_size),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

family_table |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Individuals per progeny",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )

stopifnot(
  length(family_size) == 13L,
  all(family_size == 15L)
)
```

## 6. Phenotype contract

`pheno_real.rds` is treated as the prepared phenotype object for genomic prediction. The raw annual records from 2014, 2015, and 2016 were audited separately and showed that the 195 analyzed individuals are the same `PROG 1`-`PROG 13` plants observed in all three years. The prepared `Cer` and `BM` values are not simple arithmetic means of those three annual observations; downstream models therefore consume the prepared values directly rather than recomputing annual means.

```{r phenotype-summary}
trait_summary <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(required_traits, function(trait) {
    x <- pheno[[trait]]
    data.frame(
      Trait = trait,
      N = sum(!is.na(x)),
      Missing = sum(is.na(x)),
      Mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      SD = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Min = min(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Max = max(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
)

trait_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Prepared phenotype summary",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

## 7. Genotype coding and marker quality control

The observed genotype coding is `-1, 0, 1`. For allele-frequency calculations it is converted to dosage `0, 1, 2` by adding one. No genotype values are treated as missing because the prepared matrix contains no `NA` values.

The prespecified marker filters are:

- minor allele frequency (MAF) at least 0.05;
- non-zero marker variance.

These rules are applied once here, before model-specific fitting. All downstream methods receive the same retained marker panel.

```{r marker-qc}
observed_codes <- sort(unique(as.vector(G)))

stopifnot(
  identical(as.numeric(observed_codes), c(-1, 0, 1)),
  sum(is.na(G)) == 0L,
  !anyDuplicated(colnames(G))
)

D <- G + 1
allele_frequency <- colMeans(D) / 2
maf <- pmin(allele_frequency, 1 - allele_frequency)
marker_variance <- apply(G, 2, var)

keep_marker <- maf >= 0.05 & marker_variance > 0

marker_qc <- data.frame(
  Marker = colnames(G),
  Allele_Frequency = allele_frequency,
  MAF = maf,
  Variance = marker_variance,
  Pass_MAF = maf >= 0.05,
  Pass_Variance = marker_variance > 0,
  Keep = keep_marker,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

qc_summary <- data.frame(
  Item = c(
    "Individuals",
    "Initial markers",
    "Missing genotype cells",
    "Duplicated marker names",
    "Markers with MAF < 0.05",
    "Markers with zero variance",
    "Markers failing both criteria",
    "Markers removed",
    "Markers retained"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(G),
    ncol(G),
    sum(is.na(G)),
    sum(duplicated(colnames(G))),
    sum(maf < 0.05),
    sum(marker_variance == 0),
    sum(maf < 0.05 & marker_variance == 0),
    sum(!keep_marker),
    sum(keep_marker)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

qc_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Marker quality-control summary",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

```{r qc-contract-checks}
G_qc <- G[, keep_marker, drop = FALSE]

qc_contract <- data.frame(
  Check = c(
    "195 individuals retained",
    "20,887 markers retained",
    "All retained markers have MAF >= 0.05",
    "All retained markers have positive variance",
    "No retained marker names are duplicated"
  ),
  Passed = c(
    nrow(G_qc) == 195L,
    ncol(G_qc) == 20887L,
    all(maf[keep_marker] >= 0.05),
    all(marker_variance[keep_marker] > 0),
    !anyDuplicated(colnames(G_qc))
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

qc_contract |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Frozen real-data genotype contract",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )

stopifnot(all(qc_contract$Passed))
```

The canonical real-data marker matrix therefore contains **195 individuals x 20,887 SNPs**.

Markers are not removed merely because two loci have identical genotype vectors across the 195 individuals. Distinct loci can be in complete linkage disequilibrium; identical observed signatures are therefore not interpreted as a data-quality failure by themselves.

## 8. Common object for downstream modules

```{r build-common-object}
real_common <- list(
  genotype = G_qc,
  phenotype = pheno,
  traits = required_traits,
  family = setNames(family, pheno$genotipo),
  marker_qc = marker_qc,
  metadata = list(
    dataset = "real",
    species = "Coffea arabica",
    individuals = nrow(G_qc),
    initial_markers = ncol(G),
    retained_markers = ncol(G_qc),
    genotype_coding = c(-1, 0, 1),
    dosage_conversion = "G + 1",
    maf_threshold = 0.05,
    variance_rule = "variance > 0",
    families = length(unique(family)),
    individuals_per_family = unique(as.integer(family_size))
  )
)
```

```{r save-audit-outputs, include=FALSE}
saveRDS(
  real_common,
  "output/real/audit/preprocessed_real_common.rds",
  compress = "gzip"
)

write.csv(
  marker_qc,
  "output/real/audit/real_marker_qc.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  qc_summary,
  "output/real/audit/real_qc_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  trait_summary,
  "output/real/audit/real_trait_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  family_table,
  "output/real/audit/real_family_structure.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## 9. Frozen input contract

The downstream real-data workflow uses the following fixed input contract:

- 195 aligned individuals;
- 13 progenies with 15 individuals each;
- 20,887 markers after `MAF >= 0.05` and positive-variance filtering;
- genotype coding `-1, 0, 1` retained for modeling;
- three prepared phenotype targets: `Prod.Cor`, `Cer`, and `BM`;
- no model-specific marker filtering before the common validation design is defined.

This object is the only genotype/phenotype input required by the validation, GBLUP, ANN, and model-comparison modules.
